# Democracy proxies: GDELT phrase timelines and Rooney Report toplines

Quick, citable proxy series for "health of democracy" as a public topic (how
often news and television say the words) and as a stated condition (what
survey respondents tell the Notre Dame Health of Democracy Survey). Method and
limits: [`docs/democracy-proxies.md`](../../docs/democracy-proxies.md).

**None of these series measures any effect of Anthropic on democracy.** They
measure attention and stated attitudes. Anthropic co-mention counts show only
whether the company appears near the words.

| File | What it is |
|---|---|
| `MANIFEST.tsv` | Pins: every GDELT API response and every Rooney PDF/page, with request URL, bytes, SHA-256, BLAKE3 and as-of date. The bytes live in the gitignored `.democorpus/`. GDELT responses cannot be re-requested identically later, so the saved bytes are the pin. |
| `gdelt-timelines.tsv` | One row per (source, query, mode, series, period): `value` and `unit`. DOC rows from `timelinevolraw` also carry a `(norm)` series: total articles GDELT monitored that day. **As of 2026-11-04, 17 of 24 requests are pinned**: every TV response, and the DOC `timelinevol` responses except the `democracy` control. The DOC `democracy` control and all DOC `timelinevolraw` responses hit GDELT's rate limit (HTTP 429) and are marked `NOT PINNED` in `gdelt-summary.tsv`. |
| `gdelt-summary.tsv` | Per query: resolution, first and last period, periods with a non-zero value, peak period and value, and the sum. |
| `rooney-reports.tsv` | The 13 Rooney Reports linked from the listing page: PDF SHA-256, pages, embedded images per page (charts and logos, not extracted), and any AI-use disclosure, verbatim. |
| `rooney-transcription.tsv` | **Input, hand-transcribed.** Every percent stated in report text, with group, wave as stated, the report's wording, and a verbatim quote. |
| `rooney-toplines.tsv` | **Output.** The transcription after `build` has checked each quote against the page text of the pinned PDF and each percent against its quote, with the quote's BLAKE3. |
| `rooney-questionnaire.tsv` | **Input, hand-copied.** Item stems from the two questionnaires the Institute publishes as PDFs (October 2025, May 2026). |
| `rooney-items.tsv` | **Output.** The stems after `build` has found each in the pinned questionnaire, with page numbers. |

Rebuild and check:

    uv run scripts/democracy_proxies.py fetch-gdelt  --as-of 2026-11-04   # skips anything already pinned
    uv run scripts/democracy_proxies.py fetch-rooney --as-of 2026-11-04
    uv run scripts/democracy_proxies.py build     # no network; byte-identical on rerun
    uv run scripts/democracy_proxies.py verify    # re-hash every pin, rebuild, compare bytes

A fresh `fetch-gdelt` on another day returns different bytes. That would be a
new pin, not a reproduction: keep the old `.democorpus/` to reproduce these
TSVs.

## Attribution and terms

This folder is **not** covered by the repository's CC0 dedication.

- **GDELT.** Data from the GDELT Project (https://www.gdeltproject.org/),
  DOC 2.0 and TV 2.0 APIs. GDELT's terms of use
  (https://www.gdeltproject.org/about.html) make its datasets "available for
  unlimited and unrestricted use for any academic, commercial, or governmental
  use of any kind without fee", and require that "any use or redistribution of
  the data must include a citation to the GDELT Project and a link to this
  website". This README is that citation. TV results come from captions in the
  Internet Archive's Television News Archive (https://archive.org/details/tv),
  which we credit as the underlying source. The raw responses stay in
  `.democorpus/`.
- **Rooney Reports and questionnaires.** (c) University of Notre Dame,
  Rooney Democracy Institute. This folder republishes short verbatim quotes and
  the numbers in them, with page anchors, for commentary and research. The PDFs
  are not redistributed; each is pinned by URL and SHA-256. Cite the survey as
  the Institute asks: Hall, Matthew E.K., and David E. Campbell. 2022. *Notre
  Dame health of democracy survey.* Notre Dame, IN: Rooney Democracy Institute.
  https://rooneyinstitute.nd.edu/research/health-of-democracy-survey/
# Democracy proxies: method, limits and feasibility

### Attention to democracy and stated democratic attitudes, with Anthropic as a test case

**Status: METHOD and DATA. Binds nothing.** These series measure two things:
how much news and television *talk about* the health of democracy, and what
American survey respondents *say* about democratic norms. **None of them
measures Anthropic's effect on democracy, positive or negative.** A rise or fall
in any series here says nothing about Anthropic. An Anthropic co-mention count
says only that the company's name appeared near the words.

The paper's claim to be tested is that Anthropic is positively involved with the
health of democracy. These proxies are the denominator for that test, the
background against which any Anthropic-specific evidence would have to stand
out. They are not evidence for the claim.

Version: v0.1 · 2026-11-04 · `scripts/democracy_proxies.py` · data in
[`corpus/democracy/`](../corpus/democracy/README.md).

---

## 1. What each proxy measures

| Proxy | Measures | Unit | Does not measure |
|---|---|---|---|
| GDELT DOC 2.0 phrase timelines | Share of online news articles GDELT monitors that contain a phrase | % of monitored articles per day; raw article count, plus GDELT's daily total | Whether democracy is healthy; the stance of the article; anything about articles GDELT does not monitor |
| GDELT TV 2.0 phrase timelines | Share of national-network caption airtime that contains a phrase | % of monitored 15-second caption clips per month; raw clip count | Same; also caption errors and the stations the Internet Archive records |
| Rooney Report toplines | Percent of US respondents, usually by party, agreeing with a stated democratic-norm item | Percent as printed in report text | Trends the reports do not print; anything about AI or technology companies (not asked; see §4) |

## 2. GDELT phrase timelines

### 2.1 Queries

Every query runs against both APIs, with the longest span each allows, ending at
the as-of date (2026-11-04).

| query_id | DOC 2.0 (online news) | TV 2.0 (`market:"National"`) |
|---|---|---|
| `hod` | `"health of democracy"` | `"health of democracy"` |
| `anthropic_hod` | `anthropic "health of democracy"`: both in one article | the same, in one 15-second clip |
| `anthropic_near20_democracy` / `anthropic_democracy_clip` | `near20:"anthropic democracy"`: the two words within 20 words | `anthropic democracy`: both in one 15-second clip |
| `claude_near20_democracy` / `claude_democracy_clip` | `near20:"claude democracy"` | `claude democracy` in one clip |
| `democracy` (control) | `democracy` | `democracy` |
| `anthropic` (control) | `anthropic` | `anthropic` |

Query semantics, from GDELT's documentation. DOC 2.0 ANDs terms within an article,
and `nearN:` requires the words within N words. TV 2.0 ANDs terms within a
single 15-second caption clip: "By default all of your keywords/phrases must
appear in a single 15 second clip" (GDELT TV 2.0 API announcement,
https://blog.gdeltproject.org/gdelt-2-0-television-api-debuts/). A clip is
already a proximity window of about 40 spoken words, so the TV co-mention
queries are proximity queries without an operator. `context:` (the clip plus the
clips on either side) was not used.

Modes. DOC: `timelinevol` (percent of all monitored articles) and
`timelinevolraw` (article count, with `norm` = all articles monitored that day).
TV: `timelinevol` with `datacomb=combined` (all national stations as one
series), once as the default percent of monitored airtime, and once with
`datanorm=raw` (clip counts). GDELT defines the TV percent as the matching clips
divided "by the total number of all monitored clips from that station or set of
stations over that time interval".

**Use the normalized share for comparisons over time.** GDELT's monitored
volume changes from day to day, which is what the DOC `norm` column records.
Raw counts are kept beside the share so that small-number series can be read
honestly, where one article is the difference between zero and a spike. (On
2026-11-04 the DOC raw responses could not be pinned; see §2.2.)

### 2.2 Results

**Coverage (denominator first).** 24 requests were planned: 6 queries × 2
modes × 2 APIs. **17 were pinned.** All 12 TV responses and 5 DOC
`timelinevol` responses were received. **The DOC `democracy` control and all 6
DOC `timelinevolraw` responses were not received**: GDELT's DOC API returned
HTTP 429 (rate limit) through repeated, spaced attempts on 2026-11-04, and we
stopped rather than keep hitting it. They are listed as `NOT PINNED` in
`gdelt-summary.tsv`. `fetch-gdelt` resumes where it stopped, but a later fetch
is a later observation (§2.3). Consequence: **no DOC raw article counts and no
DOC daily totals**, so DOC co-mentions below are shares and day counts, not
article counts.

- DOC: daily, 2017-01-01 to 2026-11-03. The API returned 3,547 days. The rest of
  the span is missing from GDELT's response (for example 2025 has 348 days and
  2026 has 281 of 307), not zero.
- TV: monthly, 2009-07 to **2024-10**, 184 months, national stations combined.
  Nothing after October 2024 is returned (§2.3).
- A TV response of `{}` (2 bytes) means no matching clip in the whole span.

**"Health of democracy" as a topic.**

| | DOC: mean daily share of articles | TV: national caption clips (share of airtime) |
|---|---|---|
| 2017 | 0.00099% | 1 |
| 2018 | 0.00150% | 15 |
| 2019 | 0.00169% | 5 |
| 2020 | 0.00174% | 13 |
| 2021 | 0.00228% | 20 |
| 2022 | **0.00307%** | 34 |
| 2023 | 0.00263% | 42 |
| 2024 | 0.00201% | 46 (Jan-Oct only) |
| 2025 | 0.00146% | not covered |
| 2026 (to Nov 3) | 0.00204% | not covered |

DOC means are the average of daily `timelinevol` values over the days returned.
In online news the phrase peaked in 2022 and fell back by 2025. The top single
days are 2026-09-12 (0.0794%) and 2026-09-20 (0.0720%), then 2022-01-22/23
(around the anniversary of January 6) and 2022-06-07. Without the raw response
we cannot check whether the September 2026 spikes reflect a small daily
denominator. GDELT's daily totals vary widely, so treat them as unconfirmed. On
TV, 193 clips in all, first in 2011-06, rising through 2024. The peak month is
2024-03, with 17 clips (0.0016% of airtime).

Control `democracy` on TV: 674,311 clips. The peak months are 2022-01 (15,220
clips, 1.38% of airtime), 2022-11 and 2024-01. The DOC control is not pinned.

**Anthropic co-mentions (the test).**

| Query | Result |
|---|---|
| DOC `anthropic "health of democracy"` | Non-zero on **3 days in ~10 years**: 2023-08-31, 2026-01-30, 2026-04-11, each under 0.001% of articles |
| DOC `near20:"anthropic democracy"` | Non-zero on **64 days**: 1 each in 2018 and 2020, 4 each in 2023-2025, **50 in 2026**. Peak 2026-02-28 (0.2052% of articles, an order of magnitude above any other day), then 2026-03-18 and 2026-03-01 |
| DOC `near20:"claude democracy"` | Non-zero on 1,602 days, **declining** from 320 days in 2017 to 69 in 2026. That shape is other people named Claude (Jean-Claude and others; not verified article by article), not Anthropic's model. Unusable without disambiguation |
| DOC `anthropic` (control) | Non-zero on 2,144 days; near-daily from 2023. Peak 2026-09-13 (0.5547%) |
| TV `anthropic "health of democracy"`, same clip | **0** clips, 2009-07 to 2024-10 |
| TV `anthropic democracy`, same clip | **0** clips |
| TV `claude democracy`, same clip | 17 clips in 10 months, last in 2023-03; not checked to be Anthropic's Claude |
| TV `anthropic` (control) | 828 clips: 320 in 2023, 410 in Jan-Oct 2024; peak 2023-09 (93 clips) |

What this shows: in the record GDELT monitors, Anthropic and "health of
democracy" almost never appear together, in news or on national TV. Anthropic
near "democracy" became a visible pairing only in 2026, concentrated around one
late-February episode. **These counts do not say whether that coverage credited
Anthropic, criticized it, or merely listed it.** Reading the articles would
need DOC `artlist` mode (URLs and titles), which is not built here.

### 2.3 Known weaknesses

- **"Anthropic" before 2021 is mostly the anthropic principle.** The control
  series is reported from 2017 (DOC) and 2009 (TV) without filtering. Read it
  from 2021 on.
- **"Claude" is a common first name** (Claude Monet, Claude Shannon, and
  others), so `claude` co-mentions are an upper bound.
- **DOC 2.0 searches machine-translated text** in many languages, while
  `"health of democracy"` is an English phrase. Translated articles can match.
- **TV coverage ends in October 2024.** The API accepts a 2026 end date but
  returns no months after 2024-10. The TV series therefore covers none of the
  period in which Anthropic became a household name.
- **API responses are not reproducible.** GDELT recomputes. The saved bytes in
  `.democorpus/gdelt/`, hashed in `MANIFEST.tsv`, are the only pin. A later
  fetch is a new observation, not a check.
- **TV GKG not used.** The American Television Global Knowledge Graph
  (https://blog.gdeltproject.org/announcing-the-american-television-global-knowledge-graph-tv-gkg/)
  annotates the same captions with GKG themes and entities. It would allow
  theme-coded rather than phrase-coded series, but it is a bulk dataset (files
  or BigQuery), not an API, and GDELT warns that captions carry "a high level
  of inherent noise", with person and organization names especially reduced.
  It draws on the same Internet Archive recordings, so it would add themes but
  not later months.

## 3. Rooney Reports (Notre Dame Health of Democracy Survey)

### 3.1 Source

The Rooney Democracy Institute's listing page
(https://rooneyinstitute.nd.edu/research/health-of-democracy-survey/rooney-reports/)
links 13 report PDFs, October 2024 to May 2026. All 13 are pinned, along with
the listing page itself, the survey page, and the two questionnaires the
Institute publishes as PDFs (October 2025 and May 2026 AmeriSpeak omnibus).
`fetch-rooney` checks that every PDF linked from the pinned listing page is
pinned.

The survey has run since October 2022. Its fieldwork is by NORC's AmeriSpeak
panel (R05: "fielded by NORC/UChicago via the Amerispeak panel"), and later
waves follow a panel of the same respondents (R10: N = 1,093).

### 3.2 Method: transcribe text, never charts

Each report is two pages of prose around one to three chart images. Every
percent that appears **in the text layer** was hand-transcribed into
`rooney-transcription.tsv`. Each row carries the report, page, wave as the
report states it, group, the report's wording of the item, whether that wording
is quoted or only described, the value as printed, the numeric percent, and a
verbatim quote. `build` re-extracts each page with `pypdf==5.4.0` and fails
unless:

- the quote is on the stated page (after normalizing whitespace, curly quotes
  and dashes);
- the printed value is in the quote;
- the numeric percent is in the quote.

Hedged values ("roughly 10%", "approximately 93%") keep the hedge in
`value_text` and the number in `percent`. Bounds and ranges ("Over 40%",
"19-22%", "near 4-6%") and verbal fractions ("one-in-four", "Nearly 1 in 5",
"Around 6 in 10") have an empty `percent`: converting them would be an
inference.

**Not extracted:** everything in the chart images. `rooney-reports.tsv` lists
the embedded images per page (charts and logos; 1 to 3 per page). The charts
carry figures the text omits, for example every Independent figure in R01 and
the full least-liked-group distribution in R06. They were not read and not
estimated.

Item wording. The reports paraphrase. For the October 2025 wave, the published
questionnaire gives exact stems, so `rooney-questionnaire.tsv` maps 30 report
items to questionnaire blocks, and `build` checks that each stem occurs in the
pinned questionnaire PDF (`rooney-items.tsv`, with page numbers). Earlier waves'
questionnaires are on Google Drive as codebooks and were not pinned, so for
reports drawing on 2024 and spring 2025 waves the wording is the report's own.

### 3.3 Results

There are 129 transcribed values from 13 reports, all verified against the
pinned PDFs. Most reports print no whole-sample figure, several print none for
Independents, and groups change from report to report (party, Trump vote,
Christian nationalist identity, leaners), so few items form a true series. The
ones that recur across waves, as printed:

| Item (questionnaire block) | Group | Fall 2024 | Spring 2025 | Fall 2025 | Report |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Force may be needed to save the (traditional) American way of life (MCCLDEMO B) | D / R / I | 11 / 29 / 21 | n/p | 23 / 35 / 32 | R08 |
| A time will come when patriotic Americans have to take the law into their own hands (MCCLDEMO C) | D / R / I | 10 / 26 / "around 19-22" | D 10, R ~30, I 15 (April 2025, R07) | 18 / 31 / "around 19-22" | R07, R08 |
| Federal government should declare the US a Christian nation (CHRISTNA A) | D / R / I | "near 4-6" / 31 / 12 | R 34 | 6 / 41 / 17 | R09 |
| American way of life is under attack (CIVILWAR A) | D / R | 49 / 74 | 62 / 73 | n/p | R10 |
| US is on the brink of a new civil war (CIVILWAR B) | D / R / I | 37 / 37 / 31 | 50 / 34 / 39 | n/p | R10 |
| Voting should be easy (SUPPDEMO B) | D / R / I | 94 / 81 / n/p | n/p | 93 / 78 / 79 | R01, R11 |
| President should not be above the law (SUPPDEMO G) | non-Trump / Trump voters; then D / R / I | 97 / 81 (R04; wave not stated) | n/p | 94 / 83 / 81 | R04, R11 |

n/p: not printed in report text. Fall 2025 = the October 2025 wave.

Items asked once in the pinned reports: voting rights and media shutdown (R01);
pure independents and representation (R02); strong-leader items by Trump vote
(R04, R05); least-liked groups (R06); partisan violence (R08: 2-7% agree, Fall
2025); and norm violations, fairness and tolerance (R11-R13, October 2025).

**Inconsistencies in the source, kept as printed:**

- *Force to save the way of life, Republicans.* R07 says "Over 40% of
  Republicans agreed" and calls the result stable across August 2024, November
  2024 and April 2025. R08 gives Republicans 29% in Fall 2024. The questionnaire
  item includes "traditional" (as R07 quotes it); R08 quotes it without. The
  reports do not explain the gap. Possible causes include a different agreement
  cut on the 7-point scale, a different wave, or a different weighting. Do not
  splice R07 and R08 into one series.
- *Mighty leader.* R04 gives Trump voters 66% and non-Trump voters 16%. R05,
  from the Fall 2024 wave, gives 70.8% and 16.4% for the same item. R04 states
  no wave.
- *"Fall 2024"* names both the August 2024 and the late-November 2024 fieldwork
  in different reports. `wave_as_stated` keeps each report's label and does not
  resolve it.
- *Agreement cut.* The items use a 7-point scale. Only R11 and R13 say what
  counts as agreement ("agree or strongly agree", which apparently excludes
  "somewhat agree"). The other reports do not say.
- *R13 tolerance items* are asked about the respondent's least-liked group, and
  "run for office" is asked as a ban ("should be banned from running for public
  office"). R13's "support allowing individuals to run for office" is the
  report's framing.

**An Anthropic finding inside the democracy data.** Three reports (R08
December 2025, R09 January 2026, R10 February 2026) carry an "AI transparency
statement". It begins: "Anthropic's Claude Opus 4.6 was used in initial data
analysis and identification of trends. Results reported were manually and
independently verified by the author without use of generative AI." The full
text is in `rooney-reports.tsv`. So Anthropic's product is an input to the
production of this democracy-health research. That is a fact about tool use,
disclosed by the authors. It says nothing about whether the use improved or
degraded the research. It is also the only point in these sources where
Anthropic touches democracy measurement directly. (R08 is dated December 2025
and names Opus 4.6; we did not check that model's release date against the
report date.)

### 3.4 Microdata

The survey page offers the data to researchers on request: "The Rooney
Democracy Institute is making our Health of Democracy Survey data available to
other researchers. You can review our codebooks below and fill out a request for
the data using the form below." The request is a Google Form, and the page
states no license. Codebooks for October 2022, June 2023, December 2023, August
2024, November 2024 and April 2025 are on Google Drive; October 2025 and May 2026
are on the Institute's site. **Microdata would replace this whole transcription
step**: the full 7-point distributions, every party group, and weighted
toplines for items the reports never print (for example AUTODEMO "Having a
democratic political system", asked in October 2025). The terms for publishing
derived tables are unknown until a request is answered. Ask before building on
it.

## 4. What none of these answers

- **Attention is not health.** More articles saying "health of democracy" can
  mean more threat, more advocacy, or one viral op-ed. These series count
  words.
- **Stated attitudes are not conditions.** Rooney measures what respondents say
  about norms. It does not measure institutions, elections or rights. V-Dem and
  Freedom House (§5.3) rate conditions, by expert coding.
- **No series isolates Anthropic.** The best available is a co-mention count,
  which cannot tell praise from criticism, or Anthropic's work on democracy from
  a reporter's list of AI companies.
- **Rooney asks nothing about AI or technology companies.** Neither pinned
  questionnaire mentions artificial intelligence. The only technology option is
  "Social media and misinformation", one of six answers to the new May 2026 item
  DEMOPROB ("the most important problem facing American democracy"), and no
  pinned report prints its result.
- **Causality is out of reach.** Even a perfect Anthropic-specific series would
  show association with attention, not an effect on democratic health.

## 5. Feasibility notes (not built)

Sources for this section were read on 2026-11-04 and are cited by URL, not
pinned. Anything marked "not verified" was not confirmed from a primary page.

### 5.1 The Trust Project

**What it is:** a news-credibility *standard*, not a measure of trust levels.
https://thetrustproject.org describes "an international consortium of news
organizations" whose member sites display eight Trust Indicators: Best
Practices, Journalist Expertise, Type of Work, References, Methods, Locally
Sourced, Diverse Voices, and Actionable Feedback. It reports "more than 300 news
sites" as partners.

**Time series:** none found. It publishes no member-count history and no survey.
Its FAQ (https://thetrustproject.org/faq/) cites only one-off results (Reach
Plc's own report of higher trust in The Mirror after adopting the indicators,
and a University of Texas Center for Media Engagement experiment). The only
series one could build is adopting outlets over time, reconstructed from
Wayback snapshots of the partner list (not attempted). That would count a supply
of credibility labels, not public trust. The site is "All rights reserved", and
its FAQ calls "The Trust Project and Trust Indicators" exclusive trademarks.

**Verdict:** not a democracy-health proxy. At most, an outlet-level covariate:
whether a news source carries the indicators.

### 5.2 BCG Trust Index

**Method as BCG describes it.** Sources: the 2022 article
(https://www.bcg.com/publications/2022/trust-index-analyzing-companies-trustworthiness)
and the May 2022 report *What AI Reveals About Trust in the World's Largest
Companies*
(https://web-assets.bcg.com/f5/46/c936df6540348a390708774edbb6/bcg-what-ai-reveals-about-trust-in-the-worlds-largest-companies-may-2022-2.pdf),
pp. 7-8 and the methodology appendix, pp. 31-32.

- *Dimensions:* four. **Competence** is "whether the company can effectively
  accomplish a specific task at hand". **Fairness** is "how equitable and
  empathetic the company is in delivering on its promise". **Transparency** is
  "how open and unambiguous the company's decision making and actions are".
  **Resilience** is "how effectively the company avoids or recovers from
  challenges and crises". BCG ties them to the ability, benevolence and
  integrity model (Mayer et al. 1995).
- *Data:* scraped traditional news ("leading wire services, newspapers, and
  journals") and Twitter, "more than 100,000 sources worldwide", English only
  per the article. The universe is about 1,100 public companies with market
  capitalization above $20B, over 2018-2021.
- *Mention detection:* "a list of more than 200 words derived from the academic
  literature", positive and negative, per dimension. Examples: competence
  includes credibility, capability, expertise, reliability. Fairness includes
  concern, commitment, principle, respect, values. Transparency includes
  forthrightness, accuracy, honesty, candor. Resilience includes confidence,
  control, risk management, with antonyms such as corruption, lawsuits and
  scandals.
- *Scoring:* an NLP engine (Quid) labels each trust mention positive, neutral
  or negative. Neutral mentions are discarded. For each source, the score is
  (positive − negative) / (positive + negative), on −1.0 to +1.0. Source scores
  are weighted by "strength" = sentences × potential impressions (subscribers or
  followers). On average, impressions split 91% traditional news and 9% social
  media. Scores are compared with industry benchmarks, and BCG recommends using
  the index "primarily as a relative metric, rather than as an absolute one".
- *Self-stated limits:* it measures "trusting sentiment, a proxy for trust", and
  news and social sources may overrepresent some voices and newsworthy topics.

**Updated after 2022?** No new edition of the index was found. A 2024 article
(https://www.bcg.com/publications/2024/rebuilding-corporate-trust) reuses the
approach ("real-time natural language processing to analyze news and social
media mentions and impressions") on 177 companies, Q4 2019 to Q3 2022. bcg.com
was not searched exhaustively, so this is "not found", not "none exists". No
underlying data is public.

**Extending it to Anthropic and peers with this repo's tools.** Peers: OpenAI,
Google (Alphabet), Microsoft, Meta. BCG's own universe excludes Anthropic and
OpenAI, which are private.

| BCG component | Repo substitute | Gap |
|---|---|---|
| Mention corpus: news | GDELT DOC 2.0 `artlist` mode, which returns article URLs and titles (up to 250 per call), pinned like the timelines here, then fetched article text | Needs article fetches; publisher terms vary; GDELT gives no full text |
| Mention corpus: social | Hacker News corpus (`corpus/hacker-news/`, Anthropic set already built, IDs only); peers need their own regex sets | HN is practitioners, not the public; no Twitter/X (BCG's social source is now paid API only) |
| Mention corpus: investors | Earnings-call AI corpus (`corpus/earnings-calls/`): analysts and executives talking about the peers, verbatim and anchored | Covers public companies' calls; Anthropic appears only as mentioned by others |
| 200-keyword trust lexicon | BCG publishes examples, not the list. A published, versioned regex per dimension, built from the examples and Mayer et al. | Not BCG's list, so not BCG's index. Name it differently |
| Quid sentiment (positive / neutral / negative) | The two NLI witnesses (DeBERTa-v3-large and ModernBERT-large zero-shot, `docs/earnings-call-ai-corpus.md` §5), with hypotheses per dimension and polarity ("The text says {company} is competent at ..."). A proposed label needs both witnesses ≥ 0.5 | Witness output is a proposal, never a verdict, until a stratified human gold set measures precision (`docs/bert-enrichment-spec.md` §5) |
| Impressions weighting | None free. GDELT gives no readership. HN points or comment counts are a weak stand-in | Proprietary (audience data); report unweighted and say so |
| Industry benchmark | The peer set itself (relative, as BCG advises) | Five companies is a thin benchmark |

**Proprietary parts:** Quid (the NLP engine and its theme graphs), the
traditional-news archive with impression counts, Twitter/X firehose access, and
the full keyword list. Everything else can be rebuilt from public, pinned data
with the repo's existing method. The result would be a *BCG-style* trust
sentiment index, not the BCG Trust Index, and like BCG's it would measure talk
about trust, not trust.

### 5.3 Other free proxies

| Source | What it measures | License / terms | Cadence | AI or tech? |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| V-Dem dataset (https://v-dem.net/data/the-v-dem-dataset/), v16, March 2026 | Expert-coded democracy conditions, country-year | CC BY-SA 4.0 (share-alike, so derived tables cannot sit under CC0); free download | Annual (March) | No company coverage. Has digital-society and disinformation indicators (specific variables not verified) |
| Freedom House, Freedom in the World (https://freedomhouse.org/report/freedom-world), 2026 edition | Political rights and civil liberties scores, 208 countries and territories | "free for personal, academic, and nonprofit use"; commercial use needs permission (https://freedomhouse.org/content-permissions); no open license | Annual | No. Freedom on the Net is separate (not checked) |
| Pew Research Center, public trust in government (https://www.pewresearch.org/politics/2025/12/04/public-trust-in-government-1958-2025/) | Trust in federal government, 1958-2025; 17% in September 2025 | Terms allow citation; survey data may be republished only as excerpts, and scraping is prohibited (https://www.pewresearch.org/about/terms-and-conditions/). Cite points; do not commit the full series | Irregular, several times a year | Separate AI-attitude surveys (e.g. https://www.pewresearch.org/internet/2025/09/17/how-americans-view-ai-and-its-impact-on-people-and-society/: concern rose from 37% in 2021 to 50% in 2025), not a fixed series |
| Gallup, Confidence in Institutions (https://news.gallup.com/poll/712436/confidence-institutions-remains-near-time-low.aspx) | Confidence in 15+ institutions, since 1973 (some since 1993) | Copyright Gallup, all rights reserved; reuse terms not verified; microdata licensed (not verified) | Annual (June) | **Yes, sector level:** "large technology companies" since 2020, 32% then, 20% in June 2026 (a new low). No AI item |
| Edelman Trust Barometer (https://www.edelman.com/trust) | Trust in business, government, NGOs, media; by sector; ~28 countries | Reports free to read; data terms not verified (Edelman pages returned 403 to our fetch) | Annual (January) | **Yes:** technology sector trust and "AI companies" items (2025 tech-sector brief: 56% global trust in AI companies, via secondary summary, not verified from the PDF) |

**Recommendation.** For *conditions*, V-Dem is the only open, bulk-reusable
series. Its share-alike license means derived tables go in their own folder with
their own license, like `corpus/*/` here. For *trust in the tech sector*,
Gallup's annual item is the cleanest public series. It is seven points long and
covers the sector, not any company. No free source measures trust in Anthropic
specifically. That is a finding about the evidence base, and the paper should
say so rather than fill the gap with proxies.

464 scripts/democracy_proxies.py
#!/usr/bin/env -S uv run --script
# /// script
# requires-python = ">=3.10"
# dependencies = ["blake3==1.0.11", "pypdf==5.4.0"]
# ///
"""Health-of-democracy proxies: GDELT phrase timelines and Rooney Report toplines.

These series measure ATTENTION to democracy (how often news and television use
the words) and stated CONDITIONS (what survey respondents say). None of them
measures any effect of Anthropic on democracy. See docs/democracy-proxies.md.

Two sources, each pinned by the bytes actually received:

  gdelt   GDELT TV 2.0 API (television captions, Internet Archive TV News
          Archive) and GDELT DOC 2.0 API (online news). API responses are not
          reproducible later, so every response is saved verbatim into the
          gitignored .democorpus/gdelt/ and recorded in MANIFEST.tsv with request
          URL, bytes, SHA-256, BLAKE3 and the --as-of date. The saved bytes ARE
          the pin; `fetch-gdelt` never overwrites a saved response.
  rooney  Notre Dame Rooney Democracy Institute "Rooney Reports" (Health of
          Democracy Survey). The PDFs are pinned the same way into
          .democorpus/rooney/. Toplines are HAND-TRANSCRIBED into
          corpus/democracy/rooney-transcription.tsv, each with a verbatim quote
          and page; `build` re-extracts the page text from the pinned PDF and
          fails unless every quote is on its stated page and every percent is
          in its quote. Numbers that appear only in chart images are not
          transcribed.

    uv run scripts/democracy_proxies.py fetch-gdelt  --as-of 2026-11-04
    uv run scripts/democracy_proxies.py fetch-rooney --as-of 2026-11-04
    uv run scripts/democracy_proxies.py build     # TSVs from saved bytes only; no network
    uv run scripts/democracy_proxies.py verify    # re-hash every pin; rebuild must match byte for byte

No clock, host or random id enters any output: the as-of date is an argument.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import argparse
import csv
import hashlib
import io
import json
import re
import sys
import time
import unicodedata
import urllib.error
import urllib.parse
import urllib.request
from pathlib import Path

import blake3

ROOT = Path(__file__).resolve().parent.parent
CORPUS = ROOT / "corpus" / "democracy"
BULK = ROOT / ".democorpus"                       # gitignored: every saved response and PDF
MANIFEST = CORPUS / "MANIFEST.tsv"
TRANSCRIPTION = CORPUS / "rooney-transcription.tsv"   # hand-transcribed report numbers (input)
QUESTIONNAIRE = CORPUS / "rooney-questionnaire.tsv"   # hand-copied questionnaire stems (input)
OUTPUTS = ("gdelt-timelines.tsv", "gdelt-summary.tsv", "rooney-reports.tsv", "rooney-toplines.tsv", "rooney-items.tsv")
UA = "anthropic-pbc democracy-proxies research (public CC0 research repo; contact sloane@ethicic.com)"
TSV = {"delimiter": "\t", "quoting": csv.QUOTE_NONE, "quotechar": None}   # plain TSV: no quoting, no tabs in fields
MANIFEST_COLS = ["source", "item", "path", "url", "bytes", "sha256", "blake3", "as_of"]

# ------------------------------------------------------------------ GDELT
DOC_API = "https://api.gdeltproject.org/api/v2/doc/doc"
TV_API = "https://api.gdeltproject.org/api/v2/tv/tv"
DOC_START = "20170101000000"     # DOC 2.0 timeline modes reach back to 1 January 2017
TV_START = "20090701000000"      # TV 2.0 reaches back to July 2009
TV_MARKET = 'market:"National"'  # the national networks GDELT monitors (CNN, MSNBC, FOX News, ...)
GDELT_SLEEP = 20                 # GDELT asks for at most one request every 5 seconds; stay well under

# (id, phrase query). DOC: terms are ANDed within an article; near20 requires the
# two words within 20 words of each other. TV: terms are ANDed within one
# 15-second caption clip, which is already a proximity constraint.
DOC_QUERIES = [
    ("hod", '"health of democracy"'),
    ("anthropic_hod", 'anthropic "health of democracy"'),
    ("anthropic_near20_democracy", 'near20:"anthropic democracy"'),
    ("claude_near20_democracy", 'near20:"claude democracy"'),
    ("democracy", "democracy"),
    ("anthropic", "anthropic"),
]
TV_QUERIES = [
    ("hod", '"health of democracy"'),
    ("anthropic_hod", 'anthropic "health of democracy"'),
    ("anthropic_democracy_clip", "anthropic democracy"),
    ("claude_democracy_clip", "claude democracy"),
    ("democracy", "democracy"),
    ("anthropic", "anthropic"),
]


def gdelt_requests(as_of: str) -> list[dict[str, str]]:
    end = as_of.replace("-", "") + "000000"
    out = []
    for qid, q in DOC_QUERIES:
        for mode in ("timelinevol", "timelinevolraw"):
            p = {"query": q, "mode": mode, "format": "json", "startdatetime": DOC_START, "enddatetime": end}
            out.append({"item": f"doc_{qid}_{mode}", "api": "doc", "qid": qid, "query": q, "mode": mode,
                        "url": DOC_API + "?" + urllib.parse.urlencode(p, quote_via=urllib.parse.quote)})
    for qid, q in TV_QUERIES:
        for norm in ("percent", "raw"):
            p = {"query": f"{q} {TV_MARKET}", "mode": "timelinevol", "format": "json", "datacomb": "combined",
                 "startdatetime": TV_START, "enddatetime": end}
            if norm == "raw":
                p["datanorm"] = "raw"
            out.append({"item": f"tv_{qid}_timelinevol_{norm}", "api": "tv", "qid": qid,
                        "query": f"{q} {TV_MARKET}", "mode": f"timelinevol/{norm}",
                        "url": TV_API + "?" + urllib.parse.urlencode(p, quote_via=urllib.parse.quote)})
    return out


# ------------------------------------------------------------------ Rooney
ROONEY_BASE = "https://rooneyinstitute.nd.edu"
ROONEY_PAGES = [
    ("listing", "/research/health-of-democracy-survey/rooney-reports/"),
    ("survey_page", "/research/health-of-democracy-survey/"),
]
# (report id, date as listed, title as listed, asset path) -- from the listing page pinned above.
ROONEY_REPORTS = [
    ("R01", "October 2024", "Democracy in the Balance: Partisan Perspectives on Support for Democratic Values", "/assets/590560/rooney_report_1.pdf"),
    ("R02", "November 2024", "The Representation Paradox: How Pure Independents Navigate Democratic Values", "/assets/597615/241112_rooney_report_2.pdf"),
    ("R03", "December 2024", "Christian Nationalism and Democracy: Attitudes Towards Democratic Participation and Representation", "/assets/598034/rooney_report_3.pdf"),
    ("R04", "February 2025", "Views on Democratic Principles and Leadership: Divides Between Trump and Non-Trump Voters", "/assets/612507/rooney_february.pdf"),
    ("R05", "March 2025", "Trump Voters Back Strong Leadership — But Not Radical Democratic Reform", "/assets/612503/rooney_report_5.pdf"),
    ("R06", "April 2025", "Who do Americans like least? Polarization, Consesus, and the Politics of Dislike", "/assets/613114/rooney_report_6.pdf"),
    ("R07", "September 2025", "The State of Democratic Sentiment in America", "/assets/636474/rooney_report_7_sep_2025.pdf"),
    ("R08", "December 2025", "The Growth of Support for Political Violence", "/assets/652986/rooney_report_8_dec_2025.pdf"),
    ("R09", "January 2026", "The Rising Tide of Christian Nationalism", "/assets/652984/rooney_report_9_jan_2026.pdf"),
    ("R10", "February 2026", "Post-Election Anxieties: The 2024 Election and Feelings of Threat", "/assets/652985/rooney_report_10_feb_2026.pdf"),
    ("R11", "March 2026", "Americans Agree on Democratic Principles- but Opinions Diverge on their Application", "/assets/656052/rooney_report_11_mar_2026.pdf"),
    ("R12", "April 2026", "The Fairness Divide: How Americans View Opportunity and Advantage", "/assets/656053/rooney_report_12_apr_2026.pdf"),
    ("R13", "May 2026", "Who Counts? Political Tolerance in American Democracy", "/assets/658265/rooney_report_13_may_2026_1_.pdf"),
]
# Questionnaires (no frequencies) published on the survey page; pinned for question wording.
ROONEY_CODEBOOKS = [
    ("CB_2025_10", "NDHDS October 2025 questionnaire", "/assets/661813/notredamedemocracyamerispeakomnibusoctw2docx.pdf"),
    ("CB_2026_05", "NDHDS May 2026 questionnaire", "/assets/661814/ndamerispeakomnibusmayw1docx.pdf"),
]
AI_DISCLOSURE = re.compile(r"AI transparency statement:.*?(?:discretion of the author\.|$)")


# ------------------------------------------------------------------ helpers
def sha256(b: bytes) -> str:
    return hashlib.sha256(b).hexdigest()


def b3(b: bytes) -> str:
    return blake3.blake3(b).hexdigest()


def read_manifest() -> list[dict[str, str]]:
    if not MANIFEST.exists():
        return []
    with MANIFEST.open(newline="") as f:
        return list(csv.DictReader(f, **TSV))


def write_manifest(rows: list[dict[str, str]]) -> None:
    CORPUS.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    rows = sorted(rows, key=lambda r: (r["source"], r["item"]))
    with MANIFEST.open("w", newline="") as f:
        w = csv.DictWriter(f, fieldnames=MANIFEST_COLS, **TSV, lineterminator="\n")
        w.writeheader()
        w.writerows(rows)


def http_get(url: str, tries: int = 4) -> tuple[int, bytes]:
    last: Exception | None = None
    for i in range(tries):
        try:
            with urllib.request.urlopen(urllib.request.Request(url, headers={"User-Agent": UA}), timeout=240) as r:
                return r.status, r.read()
        except urllib.error.HTTPError as e:
            last = e
            if e.code == 429 or e.code >= 500:
                wait = min(60 * 2 ** i, 300)          # 60, 120, 240, 300 ...: back off, do not hammer
                print(f"  HTTP {e.code}; waiting {wait}s", file=sys.stderr)
                time.sleep(wait)
                continue
            raise
        except (urllib.error.URLError, TimeoutError) as e:
            last = e
            wait = 30 * (i + 1)
            print(f"  {type(e).__name__}: {e}; waiting {wait}s", file=sys.stderr)
            time.sleep(wait)
    raise RuntimeError(f"giving up on {url}: {last}")


def pin(source: str, item: str, rel: str, url: str, as_of: str, sleep: float) -> bool:
    """Fetch url into BULK/rel unless already pinned; record it in MANIFEST. Returns True if fetched."""
    rows = read_manifest()
    have = {(r["source"], r["item"]) for r in rows}
    dst = BULK / rel
    if (source, item) in have and dst.exists():
        return False
    status, body = http_get(url)
    if source == "gdelt":
        try:
            json.loads(body)
        except ValueError:
            raise RuntimeError(f"{item}: response is not JSON (first bytes: {body[:120]!r}); not pinned")
    dst.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    dst.write_bytes(body)
    rows = [r for r in rows if (r["source"], r["item"]) != (source, item)]
    rows.append({"source": source, "item": item, "path": rel, "url": url, "bytes": str(len(body)),
                 "sha256": sha256(body), "blake3": b3(body), "as_of": as_of})
    write_manifest(rows)
    print(f"  pinned {item}: {len(body)} bytes")
    time.sleep(sleep)
    return True


def norm_text(s: str) -> str:
    s = unicodedata.normalize("NFKC", s)
    s = (s.replace("’", "'").replace("‘", "'").replace("“", '"').replace("”", '"')
          .replace("–", "-").replace("—", "-").replace("­", "").replace("​", ""))
    return re.sub(r"\s+", " ", s).strip()


def write_tsv(path: Path, header: list[str], rows: list[list[str]]) -> bytes:
    buf = io.StringIO()
    w = csv.writer(buf, **TSV, lineterminator="\n")
    w.writerow(header)
    w.writerows(rows)
    data = buf.getvalue().encode("utf-8")
    path.write_bytes(data)
    return data


# ------------------------------------------------------------------ fetch
def cmd_fetch_gdelt(as_of: str) -> int:
    # TV first: the DOC API rate-limits harder, and a DOC stall should not block the TV pins.
    prio = ["anthropic_hod", "anthropic_near20_democracy", "claude_near20_democracy", "anthropic", "democracy", "hod"]
    reqs = sorted(gdelt_requests(as_of), key=lambda r: (r["api"] != "tv", r["mode"].endswith("raw"),
                                                      prio.index(r["qid"]) if r["qid"] in prio else -1))
    for r in reqs:
        print(r["item"], flush=True)
        try:
            pin("gdelt", r["item"], f"gdelt/{r['item']}.json", r["url"], as_of, GDELT_SLEEP)
        except RuntimeError as e:   # stop rather than keep hitting a rate-limited API; rerun resumes
            print(f"STOPPED at {r['item']}: {e}", file=sys.stderr)
            return 1
    print(f"ok: {len(reqs)} GDELT responses pinned")
    return 0


def cmd_fetch_rooney(as_of: str) -> int:
    for item, path in ROONEY_PAGES:
        pin("rooney", item, f"rooney/{item}.html", ROONEY_BASE + path, as_of, 2)
    for rid, _, _, path in ROONEY_REPORTS:
        pin("rooney", rid, f"rooney/{rid}_{Path(path).name}", ROONEY_BASE + path, as_of, 2)
    for cid, _, path in ROONEY_CODEBOOKS:
        pin("rooney", cid, f"rooney/{cid}_{Path(path).name}", ROONEY_BASE + path, as_of, 2)
    # Cross-check: every PDF linked from the pinned listing page is in ROONEY_REPORTS.
    listing = (BULK / "rooney/listing.html").read_text("utf-8", "replace")
    linked = sorted(set(re.findall(r'href="(/assets/[^"]+\.pdf)"', listing)))
    known = {p for *_, p in ROONEY_REPORTS}
    missing = [p for p in linked if p not in known]
    if missing:
        print(f"WARNING: listing links PDFs not in ROONEY_REPORTS: {missing}", file=sys.stderr)
        return 1
    print(f"ok: {len(ROONEY_REPORTS)} reports (= {len(linked)} PDFs linked from the listing) and "
          f"{len(ROONEY_CODEBOOKS)} questionnaires pinned")
    return 0


# ------------------------------------------------------------------ build
def load_pinned(source: str, item: str) -> bytes:
    for r in read_manifest():
        if r["source"] == source and r["item"] == item:
            b = (BULK / r["path"]).read_bytes()
            if sha256(b) != r["sha256"] or b3(b) != r["blake3"] or len(b) != int(r["bytes"]):
                raise RuntimeError(f"{source}/{item}: saved bytes do not match MANIFEST")
            return b
    raise KeyError(f"{source}/{item} not pinned; run fetch-{source}")


def fmt(v: float) -> str:
    s = f"{v:.6f}".rstrip("0").rstrip(".")
    return s if s else "0"


def build_gdelt(as_of: str) -> dict[str, bytes]:
    rows: list[list[str]] = []
    summ: list[list[str]] = []
    for r in gdelt_requests(as_of):
        try:
            d = json.loads(load_pinned("gdelt", r["item"]))
        except KeyError:          # never received (rate-limited): reported, not silently dropped
            summ.append([r["api"], r["qid"], r["query"], r["mode"], "NOT PINNED", "", "", "", "", "0", "0",
                         "", "", "", "", ""])
            continue
        timeline = d.get("timeline", [])
        if r["api"] == "doc":
            unit = "pct_of_monitored_articles" if r["mode"] == "timelinevol" else "articles"
        else:
            unit = "pct_of_monitored_airtime" if r["mode"].endswith("percent") else "caption_clips_15s"
        res = (d.get("query_details") or {}).get("date_resolution", "")
        for s in timeline:
            series = s.get("series", "")
            pts = s.get("data", [])
            for p in pts:
                date = p["date"][:8]
                rows.append([r["api"], r["qid"], r["query"], r["mode"], series, date, fmt(float(p["value"])), unit])
                if "norm" in p:
                    rows.append([r["api"], r["qid"], r["query"], r["mode"], series + " (norm)", date,
                                 fmt(float(p["norm"])), "articles_monitored_total"])
            nz = [p for p in pts if float(p["value"]) > 0]
            peak = max(pts, key=lambda p: (float(p["value"]), p["date"])) if pts else None
            summ.append([r["api"], r["qid"], r["query"], r["mode"], series, unit, res,
                         pts[0]["date"][:8] if pts else "", pts[-1]["date"][:8] if pts else "",
                         str(len(pts)), str(len(nz)),
                         nz[0]["date"][:8] if nz else "", nz[-1]["date"][:8] if nz else "",
                         peak["date"][:8] if peak and nz else "", fmt(float(peak["value"])) if peak and nz else "0",
                         fmt(sum(float(p["value"]) for p in pts))])
        if not timeline:
            summ.append([r["api"], r["qid"], r["query"], r["mode"], "", unit, res, "", "", "0", "0", "", "", "", "0", "0"])
    rows.sort(key=lambda x: (x[0], x[1], x[3], x[4], x[5]))
    summ.sort(key=lambda x: (x[0], x[1], x[3], x[4]))
    out = {}
    out["gdelt-timelines.tsv"] = write_tsv(CORPUS / "gdelt-timelines.tsv",
        ["source", "query_id", "query", "mode", "series", "date", "value", "unit"], rows)
    out["gdelt-summary.tsv"] = write_tsv(CORPUS / "gdelt-summary.tsv",
        ["source", "query_id", "query", "mode", "series", "unit", "resolution", "first_period", "last_period",
         "n_periods", "n_nonzero", "first_nonzero", "last_nonzero", "peak_period", "peak_value", "sum_value"], summ)
    return out


def pdf_pages(b: bytes) -> tuple[list[str], list[int]]:
    from pypdf import PdfReader
    rd = PdfReader(io.BytesIO(b))
    texts, imgs = [], []
    for p in rd.pages:
        texts.append(norm_text(p.extract_text() or ""))
        try:
            imgs.append(len(p.images))
        except Exception:
            imgs.append(-1)
    return texts, imgs


def build_rooney() -> dict[str, bytes]:
    pages: dict[str, list[str]] = {}
    rep_rows = []
    for rid, date, title, path in ROONEY_REPORTS:
        raw = load_pinned("rooney", rid)
        texts, imgs = pdf_pages(raw)
        pages[rid] = texts
        disc, disc_page = "", ""
        for i, t in enumerate(texts, 1):
            m = AI_DISCLOSURE.search(t)
            if m:
                disc, disc_page = m.group(0), str(i)
        rep_rows.append([rid, date, title, ROONEY_BASE + path, sha256(raw), str(len(texts)),
                         ";".join(str(n) for n in imgs), disc_page, disc])
    with TRANSCRIPTION.open(newline="") as f:
        trans = list(csv.DictReader(f, **TSV))
    top_rows, errors = [], []
    for i, t in enumerate(trans, 2):
        rid, pg = t["report"], int(t["page"])
        quote = norm_text(t["quote"])
        text = pages[rid][pg - 1] if 0 < pg <= len(pages[rid]) else ""
        if quote not in text:
            found = [str(j) for j, x in enumerate(pages[rid], 1) if quote in x]
            errors.append(f"line {i} {rid} p{pg}: quote not on page (found on: {found or 'none'}): {quote!r}")
            continue
        vt = norm_text(t["value_text"])
        if vt not in quote:
            errors.append(f"line {i}: value_text {vt!r} not in quote")
        if t["percent"] and not re.search(r"(?<![\d.])" + re.escape(t["percent"]) + r"(?![\d.])", quote):
            errors.append(f"line {i}: percent {t['percent']} not in quote")
        top_rows.append([rid, t["page"], t["wave_as_stated"], t["group"], t["item"], t["wording_in_report"],
                         t["wording_kind"], t["response"], t["value_text"], t["percent"], quote,
                         blake3.blake3(quote.encode()).hexdigest()])
    # Questionnaire wording: each hand-copied stem must occur in the pinned questionnaire PDF.
    cb_pages = {cid: pdf_pages(load_pinned("rooney", cid))[0] for cid, _, _ in ROONEY_CODEBOOKS}
    item_rows = []
    with QUESTIONNAIRE.open(newline="") as f:
        for i, q in enumerate(csv.DictReader(f, **TSV), 2):
            stem = norm_text(q["stem_quote"])
            found = [str(j) for j, x in enumerate(cb_pages[q["codebook"]], 1) if stem in x]
            if not found:
                errors.append(f"questionnaire line {i}: stem not in {q['codebook']}: {stem!r}")
                continue
            item_rows.append([q["item"], q["codebook"], q["block"], q["letter"], ";".join(found), stem,
                              blake3.blake3(stem.encode()).hexdigest(), q["note"]])
    if errors:
        raise RuntimeError("transcription check failed:\n  " + "\n  ".join(errors))
    order = {r[0]: i for i, r in enumerate(ROONEY_REPORTS)}
    top_rows.sort(key=lambda r: (order[r[0]], int(r[1]), r[4], r[3], r[2]))
    out = {}
    out["rooney-reports.tsv"] = write_tsv(CORPUS / "rooney-reports.tsv",
        ["report", "date_listed", "title_listed", "url", "pdf_sha256", "pages", "images_per_page",
         "ai_disclosure_page", "ai_disclosure_verbatim"], rep_rows)
    out["rooney-toplines.tsv"] = write_tsv(CORPUS / "rooney-toplines.tsv",
        ["report", "page", "wave_as_stated", "group", "item", "wording_in_report", "wording_kind", "response",
         "value_text", "percent", "quote_normalised", "quote_blake3"], top_rows)
    out["rooney-items.tsv"] = write_tsv(CORPUS / "rooney-items.tsv",
        ["item", "codebook", "block", "letter", "pages", "stem_normalised", "stem_blake3", "note"], item_rows)
    return out


def cmd_build(as_of: str) -> dict[str, bytes]:
    out = build_gdelt(as_of)
    out.update(build_rooney())
    for k, v in out.items():
        print(f"  {k}: {v.count(b'\n') - 1} rows, sha256 {sha256(v)[:16]}")
    return out


def cmd_verify(as_of: str) -> int:
    bad = 0
    rows = read_manifest()
    for r in rows:
        p = BULK / r["path"]
        if not p.exists():
            print(f"MISSING {r['path']}")
            bad += 1
            continue
        b = p.read_bytes()
        if len(b) != int(r["bytes"]) or sha256(b) != r["sha256"] or b3(b) != r["blake3"]:
            print(f"MISMATCH {r['path']}")
            bad += 1
    before = {n: (CORPUS / n).read_bytes() for n in OUTPUTS if (CORPUS / n).exists()}
    after = cmd_build(as_of)
    for n, b in after.items():
        if before.get(n) != b:
            print(f"NOT BYTE-IDENTICAL on rebuild: {n}")
            bad += 1
    print(f"{'ok' if not bad else 'FAIL'}: {len(rows)} pins re-hashed, {len(after)} outputs rebuilt, {bad} problems")
    return 1 if bad else 0


def as_of_from_manifest() -> str:
    vals = sorted({r["as_of"] for r in read_manifest()})
    if len(vals) != 1:
        raise SystemExit(f"expected one as-of in MANIFEST, found {vals}")
    return vals[0]


def main() -> int:
    ap = argparse.ArgumentParser(description=__doc__, formatter_class=argparse.RawDescriptionHelpFormatter)
    sub = ap.add_subparsers(dest="cmd", required=True)
    for c in ("fetch-gdelt", "fetch-rooney"):
        sp = sub.add_parser(c)
        sp.add_argument("--as-of", required=True, help="recorded fetch date, YYYY-MM-DD (also the GDELT end date)")
    sub.add_parser("build")
    sub.add_parser("verify")
    a = ap.parse_args()
    if a.cmd == "fetch-gdelt":
        return cmd_fetch_gdelt(a.as_of)
    if a.cmd == "fetch-rooney":
        return cmd_fetch_rooney(a.as_of)
    if a.cmd == "build":
        cmd_build(as_of_from_manifest())
        return 0
    return cmd_verify(as_of_from_manifest())


if __name__ == "__main__":
    sys.exit(main())

# ------------------------------------------------------------------ Rooney

ROONEY_PAGES = [

# (report id, date as listed, title as listed, asset path) -- from the listing page pinned above.
ROONEY_REPORTS = [

ROONEY_CODEBOOKS = [

AI_DISCLOSURE = re.compile(r"AI transparency statement:.*?(?:discretion of the author\.|$)")


# ------------------------------------------------------------------ helpers
def sha256(b: bytes) -> str:
    return hashlib.sha256(b).hexdigest()


def b3(b: bytes) -> str:
    return blake3.blake3(b).hexdigest()


def read_manifest() -> list[dict[str, str]]:
    if not MANIFEST.exists():
        return []
    with MANIFEST.open(newline="") as f:
        return list(csv.DictReader(f, **TSV))


def write_manifest(rows: list[dict[str, str]]) -> None:
    CORPUS.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    rows = sorted(rows, key=lambda r: (r["source"], r["item"]))
    with MANIFEST.open("w", newline="") as f:
        w = csv.DictWriter(f, fieldnames=MANIFEST_COLS, **TSV, lineterminator="\n")
        w.writeheader()
        w.writerows(rows)


def http_get(url: str, tries: int = 4) -> tuple[int, bytes]:
    last: Exception | None = None
    for i in range(tries):
        try:
            with urllib.request.urlopen(urllib.request.Request(url, headers={"User-Agent": UA}), timeout=240) as r:
                return r.status, r.read()
        except urllib.error.HTTPError as e:
            last = e
            if e.code == 429 or e.code >= 500:
                wait = min(60 * 2 ** i, 300)          # 60, 120, 240, 300 ...: back off, do not hammer
                print(f"  HTTP {e.code}; waiting {wait}s", file=sys.stderr)
                time.sleep(wait)
                continue
            raise
        except (urllib.error.URLError, TimeoutError) as e:
            last = e
            wait = 30 * (i + 1)
            print(f"  {type(e).__name__}: {e}; waiting {wait}s", file=sys.stderr)
            time.sleep(wait)
    raise RuntimeError(f"giving up on {url}: {last}")


def pin(source: str, item: str, rel: str, url: str, as_of: str, sleep: float) -> bool:
    """Fetch url into BULK/rel unless already pinned; record it in MANIFEST. Returns True if fetched."""
    rows = read_manifest()
    have = {(r["source"], r["item"]) for r in rows}
    dst = BULK / rel
    if (source, item) in have and dst.exists():
        return False
    status, body = http_get(url)
    if source == "gdelt":
        try:
            json.loads(body)
        except ValueError:
            raise RuntimeError(f"{item}: response is not JSON (first bytes: {body[:120]!r}); not pinned")
    dst.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    dst.write_bytes(body)
    rows = [r for r in rows if (r["source"], r["item"]) != (source, item)]
    rows.append({"source": source, "item": item, "path": rel, "url": url, "bytes": str(len(body)),
                 "sha256": sha256(body), "blake3": b3(body), "as_of": as_of})
    write_manifest(rows)
    print(f"  pinned {item}: {len(body)} bytes")
    time.sleep(sleep)
    return True


def norm_text(s: str) -> str:
    s = unicodedata.normalize("NFKC", s)
    s = (s.replace("’", "'").replace("‘", "'").replace("“", '"').replace("”", '"')
          .replace("–", "-").replace("—", "-").replace("­", "").replace("​", ""))
    return re.sub(r"\s+", " ", s).strip()


def write_tsv(path: Path, header: list[str], rows: list[list[str]]) -> bytes:
    buf = io.StringIO()
    w = csv.writer(buf, **TSV, lineterminator="\n")
    w.writerow(header)
    w.writerows(rows)
    data = buf.getvalue().encode("utf-8")
    path.write_bytes(data)
    return data


# ------------------------------------------------------------------ fetch
def cmd_fetch_gdelt(as_of: str) -> int:
    # TV first: the DOC API rate-limits harder, and a DOC stall should not block the TV pins.
    prio = ["anthropic_hod", "anthropic_near20_democracy", "claude_near20_democracy", "anthropic", "democracy", "hod"]
    reqs = sorted(gdelt_requests(as_of), key=lambda r: (r["api"] != "tv", r["mode"].endswith("raw"),
                                                      prio.index(r["qid"]) if r["qid"] in prio else -1))
    for r in reqs:
        print(r["item"], flush=True)
        try:
            pin("gdelt", r["item"], f"gdelt/{r['item']}.json", r["url"], as_of, GDELT_SLEEP)
        except RuntimeError as e:   # stop rather than keep hitting a rate-limited API; rerun resumes
            print(f"STOPPED at {r['item']}: {e}", file=sys.stderr)
            return 1
    print(f"ok: {len(reqs)} GDELT responses pinned")
    return 0


def cmd_fetch_rooney(as_of: str) -> int:
    for item, path in ROONEY_PAGES:
        pin("rooney", item, f"rooney/{item}.html", ROONEY_BASE + path, as_of, 2)
    for rid, _, _, path in ROONEY_REPORTS:
        pin("rooney", rid, f"rooney/{rid}_{Path(path).name}", ROONEY_BASE + path, as_of, 2)
    for cid, _, path in ROONEY_CODEBOOKS:
        pin("rooney", cid, f"rooney/{cid}_{Path(path).name}", ROONEY_BASE + path, as_of, 2)
    # Cross-check: every PDF linked from the pinned listing page is in ROONEY_REPORTS.
    listing = (BULK / "rooney/listing.html").read_text("utf-8", "replace")
    linked = sorted(set(re.findall(r'href="(/assets/[^"]+\.pdf)"', listing)))
    known = {p for *_, p in ROONEY_REPORTS}
    missing = [p for p in linked if p not in known]
    if missing:
        print(f"WARNING: listing links PDFs not in ROONEY_REPORTS: {missing}", file=sys.stderr)
        return 1
    print(f"ok: {len(ROONEY_REPORTS)} reports (= {len(linked)} PDFs linked from the listing) and "
          f"{len(ROONEY_CODEBOOKS)} questionnaires pinned")
    return 0


# ------------------------------------------------------------------ build
def load_pinned(source: str, item: str) -> bytes:
    for r in read_manifest():
        if r["source"] == source and r["item"] == item:
            b = (BULK / r["path"]).read_bytes()
            if sha256(b) != r["sha256"] or b3(b) != r["blake3"] or len(b) != int(r["bytes"]):
                raise RuntimeError(f"{source}/{item}: saved bytes do not match MANIFEST")
            return b
    raise KeyError(f"{source}/{item} not pinned; run fetch-{source}")


def fmt(v: float) -> str:
    s = f"{v:.6f}".rstrip("0").rstrip(".")
    return s if s else "0"


def build_gdelt(as_of: str) -> dict[str, bytes]:
    rows: list[list[str]] = []
    summ: list[list[str]] = []
    for r in gdelt_requests(as_of):
        try:
            d = json.loads(load_pinned("gdelt", r["item"]))
        except KeyError:          # never received (rate-limited): reported, not silently dropped
            summ.append([r["api"], r["qid"], r["query"], r["mode"], "NOT PINNED", "", "", "", "", "0", "0",
                         "", "", "", "", ""])
            continue
        timeline = d.get("timeline", [])
        if r["api"] == "doc":
            unit = "pct_of_monitored_articles" if r["mode"] == "timelinevol" else "articles"
        else:
            unit = "pct_of_monitored_airtime" if r["mode"].endswith("percent") else "caption_clips_15s"
        res = (d.get("query_details") or {}).get("date_resolution", "")
        for s in timeline:
            series = s.get("series", "")
            pts = s.get("data", [])
            for p in pts:
                date = p["date"][:8]
                rows.append([r["api"], r["qid"], r["query"], r["mode"], series, date, fmt(float(p["value"])), unit])
                if "norm" in p:
                    rows.append([r["api"], r["qid"], r["query"], r["mode"], series + " (norm)", date,
                                 fmt(float(p["norm"])), "articles_monitored_total"])
            nz = [p for p in pts if float(p["value"]) > 0]
            peak = max(pts, key=lambda p: (float(p["value"]), p["date"])) if pts else None
            summ.append([r["api"], r["qid"], r["query"], r["mode"], series, unit, res,
                         pts[0]["date"][:8] if pts else "", pts[-1]["date"][:8] if pts else "",
                         str(len(pts)), str(len(nz)),
                         nz[0]["date"][:8] if nz else "", nz[-1]["date"][:8] if nz else "",
                         peak["date"][:8] if peak and nz else "", fmt(float(peak["value"])) if peak and nz else "0",
                         fmt(sum(float(p["value"]) for p in pts))])
        if not timeline:
            summ.append([r["api"], r["qid"], r["query"], r["mode"], "", unit, res, "", "", "0", "0", "", "", "", "0", "0"])
    rows.sort(key=lambda x: (x[0], x[1], x[3], x[4], x[5]))
    summ.sort(key=lambda x: (x[0], x[1], x[3], x[4]))
    out = {}
    out["gdelt-timelines.tsv"] = write_tsv(CORPUS / "gdelt-timelines.tsv",
        ["source", "query_id", "query", "mode", "series", "date", "value", "unit"], rows)
    out["gdelt-summary.tsv"] = write_tsv(CORPUS / "gdelt-summary.tsv",
        ["source", "query_id", "query", "mode", "series", "unit", "resolution", "first_period", "last_period",
         "n_periods", "n_nonzero", "first_nonzero", "last_nonzero", "peak_period", "peak_value", "sum_value"], summ)
    return out


def pdf_pages(b: bytes) -> tuple[list[str], list[int]]:
    from pypdf import PdfReader
    rd = PdfReader(io.BytesIO(b))
    texts, imgs = [], []
    for p in rd.pages:
        texts.append(norm_text(p.extract_text() or ""))
        try:
            imgs.append(len(p.images))
        except Exception:
            imgs.append(-1)
    return texts, imgs


def build_rooney() -> dict[str, bytes]:
    pages: dict[str, list[str]] = {}
    rep_rows = []
    for rid, date, title, path in ROONEY_REPORTS:
        raw = load_pinned("rooney", rid)
        texts, imgs = pdf_pages(raw)
        pages[rid] = texts
        disc, disc_page = "", ""
        for i, t in enumerate(texts, 1):
            m = AI_DISCLOSURE.search(t)
            if m:
                disc, disc_page = m.group(0), str(i)
        rep_rows.append([rid, date, title, ROONEY_BASE + path, sha256(raw), str(len(texts)),
                         ";".join(str(n) for n in imgs), disc_page, disc])
    with TRANSCRIPTION.open(newline="") as f:
        trans = list(csv.DictReader(f, **TSV))
    top_rows, errors = [], []
    for i, t in enumerate(trans, 2):
        rid, pg = t["report"], int(t["page"])
        quote = norm_text(t["quote"])
        text = pages[rid][pg - 1] if 0 < pg <= len(pages[rid]) else ""
        if quote not in text:
            found = [str(j) for j, x in enumerate(pages[rid], 1) if quote in x]
            errors.append(f"line {i} {rid} p{pg}: quote not on page (found on: {found or 'none'}): {quote!r}")
            continue
        vt = norm_text(t["value_text"])
        if vt not in quote:
            errors.append(f"line {i}: value_text {vt!r} not in quote")
        if t["percent"] and not re.search(r"(?<![\d.])" + re.escape(t["percent"]) + r"(?![\d.])", quote):
            errors.append(f"line {i}: percent {t['percent']} not in quote")
        top_rows.append([rid, t["page"], t["wave_as_stated"], t["group"], t["item"], t["wording_in_report"],
                         t["wording_kind"], t["response"], t["value_text"], t["percent"], quote,
                         blake3.blake3(quote.encode()).hexdigest()])
    # Questionnaire wording: each hand-copied stem must occur in the pinned questionnaire PDF.
    cb_pages = {cid: pdf_pages(load_pinned("rooney", cid))[0] for cid, _, _ in ROONEY_CODEBOOKS}
    item_rows = []
    with QUESTIONNAIRE.open(newline="") as f:
        for i, q in enumerate(csv.DictReader(f, **TSV), 2):
            stem = norm_text(q["stem_quote"])
            found = [str(j) for j, x in enumerate(cb_pages[q["codebook"]], 1) if stem in x]
            if not found:
                errors.append(f"questionnaire line {i}: stem not in {q['codebook']}: {stem!r}")
                continue
            item_rows.append([q["item"], q["codebook"], q["block"], q["letter"], ";".join(found), stem,
                              blake3.blake3(stem.encode()).hexdigest(), q["note"]])
    if errors:
        raise RuntimeError("transcription check failed:\n  " + "\n  ".join(errors))
    order = {r[0]: i for i, r in enumerate(ROONEY_REPORTS)}
    top_rows.sort(key=lambda r: (order[r[0]], int(r[1]), r[4], r[3], r[2]))
    out = {}
    out["rooney-reports.tsv"] = write_tsv(CORPUS / "rooney-reports.tsv",
        ["report", "date_listed", "title_listed", "url", "pdf_sha256", "pages", "images_per_page",
         "ai_disclosure_page", "ai_disclosure_verbatim"], rep_rows)
    out["rooney-toplines.tsv"] = write_tsv(CORPUS / "rooney-toplines.tsv",
        ["report", "page", "wave_as_stated", "group", "item", "wording_in_report", "wording_kind", "response",
         "value_text", "percent", "quote_normalised", "quote_blake3"], top_rows)
    out["rooney-items.tsv"] = write_tsv(CORPUS / "rooney-items.tsv",
        ["item", "codebook", "block", "letter", "pages", "stem_normalised", "stem_blake3", "note"], item_rows)
    return out


def cmd_build(as_of: str) -> dict[str, bytes]:
    out = build_gdelt(as_of)
    out.update(build_rooney())
    for k, v in out.items():
        print(f"  {k}: {v.count(b'\n') - 1} rows, sha256 {sha256(v)[:16]}")
    return out


def cmd_verify(as_of: str) -> int:
    bad = 0
    rows = read_manifest()
    for r in rows:
        p = BULK / r["path"]
        if not p.exists():
            print(f"MISSING {r['path']}")
            bad += 1
            continue
        b = p.read_bytes()
        if len(b) != int(r["bytes"]) or sha256(b) != r["sha256"] or b3(b) != r["blake3"]:
            print(f"MISMATCH {r['path']}")
            bad += 1
    before = {n: (CORPUS / n).read_bytes() for n in OUTPUTS if (CORPUS / n).exists()}
    after = cmd_build(as_of)
    for n, b in after.items():
        if before.get(n) != b:
            print(f"NOT BYTE-IDENTICAL on rebuild: {n}")
            bad += 1
    print(f"{'ok' if not bad else 'FAIL'}: {len(rows)} pins re-hashed, {len(after)} outputs rebuilt, {bad} problems")
    return 1 if bad else 0


def as_of_from_manifest() -> str:
    vals = sorted({r["as_of"] for r in read_manifest()})
    if len(vals) != 1:
        raise SystemExit(f"expected one as-of in MANIFEST, found {vals}")
    return vals[0]


def main() -> int:
    ap = argparse.ArgumentParser(description=__doc__, formatter_class=argparse.RawDescriptionHelpFormatter)
    sub = ap.add_subparsers(dest="cmd", required=True)
    for c in ("fetch-gdelt", "fetch-rooney"):
        sp = sub.add_parser(c)
        sp.add_argument("--as-of", required=True, help="recorded fetch date, YYYY-MM-DD (also the GDELT end date)")
    sub.add_parser("build")
    sub.add_parser("verify")
    a = ap.parse_args()
    if a.cmd == "fetch-gdelt":
        return cmd_fetch_gdelt(a.as_of)
    if a.cmd == "fetch-rooney":
        return cmd_fetch_rooney(a.as_of)
    if a.cmd == "build":
        cmd_build(as_of_from_manifest())
        return 0
    return cmd_verify(as_of_from_manifest())


if __name__ == "__main__":
    sys.exit(main())

# Metadata for snapshot://ethicalcapital/v0.1/codebook_questions (schema/metadata.schema.yml)
producer: Ethical Capital (this repository)
title: Analyst-question intent codebook v0.1
description: >-
  Ten hand-written natural-language hypotheses that the NLI witnesses score
  against every AI analyst question, in five groups: commercial (q_revenue,
  q_efficiency), capital (q_spend), threat (q_competition), workforce
  (q_workforce) and oversight (q_risk, q_controls, q_regulation, q_harm,

# Metadata for data://garden/democracy/2026-11-04/proxies (schema/metadata.schema.yml)
title: Health-of-democracy proxies, GDELT phrase timelines and Rooney Report toplines, as of 2026-11-04
description: >-
  Two kinds of proxy for "health of democracy". GDELT timelines measure
  attention: the share of monitored online news (DOC 2.0) and of national TV
  caption airtime (TV 2.0) that contains a phrase, including Anthropic
  co-mention queries. Rooney toplines are stated attitudes: percents of US
  respondents printed in the text of the Notre Dame Health of Democracy Survey's
  Rooney Reports, each checked against the pinned PDF. None of these series
  measures any effect of Anthropic on democracy. Method and limits in
  docs/democracy-proxies.md.
processing: >-
  `build` reads only saved bytes (no network) and fails if any saved file's
  size, SHA-256 or BLAKE3 differs from MANIFEST.tsv. GDELT: for each of the 24
  planned requests, every timeline point becomes one row of gdelt-timelines.tsv
  (date truncated to YYYYMMDD; value formatted to at most 6 decimals) and each
  series one row of gdelt-summary.tsv; a request never received is kept as a
  NOT PINNED summary row, not dropped, and a `{}` response (no matching clip)
  as an empty-series row. DOC timelinevolraw rows would carry a "(norm)"
  series (GDELT's daily total), but none were pinned. Rooney: each pinned
  report PDF is re-extracted page by page with pypdf 5.4.0 and normalised (NFKC,
  curly quotes, dashes, soft hyphens, whitespace); rooney-reports.tsv records
  page and embedded-image counts and any "AI transparency statement".
  Each hand-transcribed row is checked: the quote must be on its stated page,
  value_text in the quote, and percent in the quote; each hand-copied stem must
  occur in its pinned questionnaire. Any failure stops the build, so the
  toplines and items hold every input row. Drops: chart images (counted, never
  read or estimated), GDELT article and clip text (never requested; no artlist
  mode), and the 7 GDELT requests that returned HTTP 429 (no data, reported as
  NOT PINNED).
unit_of_analysis: >-
  gdelt-timelines.tsv: one (source, query, mode, series, period) value;

  rooney-items.tsv: one questionnaire item stem.
denominator: >-

  attention: the share of monitored online news (DOC 2.0) and of national TV
  caption airtime (TV 2.0) that contains a phrase, including Anthropic
  co-mention queries. Rooney toplines are stated attitudes: percents of US
  respondents printed in the text of the Notre Dame Health of Democracy Survey's
  Rooney Reports, each checked against the pinned PDF. None of these series
  measures any effect of Anthropic on democracy. Method and limits in
  docs/democracy-proxies.md.
processing: >-

  size, SHA-256 or BLAKE3 differs from MANIFEST.tsv. GDELT: for each of the 24
  planned requests, every timeline point becomes one row of gdelt-timelines.tsv
  (date truncated to YYYYMMDD; value formatted to at most 6 decimals) and each
  series one row of gdelt-summary.tsv; a request never received is kept as a
  NOT PINNED summary row, not dropped, and a `{}` response (no matching clip)
  as an empty-series row. DOC timelinevolraw rows would carry a "(norm)"
  series (GDELT's daily total), but none were pinned. Rooney: each pinned
  report PDF is re-extracted page by page with pypdf 5.4.0 and normalised (NFKC,
  curly quotes, dashes, soft hyphens, whitespace); rooney-reports.tsv records
  page and embedded-image counts and any "AI transparency statement".
  Each hand-transcribed row is checked: the quote must be on its stated page,
  value_text in the quote, and percent in the quote; each hand-copied stem must
  occur in its pinned questionnaire. Any failure stops the build, so the
  toplines and items hold every input row. Drops: chart images (counted, never
  read or estimated), GDELT article and clip text (never requested; no artlist
  mode), and the 7 GDELT requests that returned HTTP 429 (no data, reported as
  NOT PINNED).

  values (text layer only; chart figures not extracted); 30 questionnaire stems
  (29 October 2025, 1 May 2026). Earlier waves' questionnaires were not pinned.
  As of 2026-11-04.

  - "Whether democracy is healthy: attention is not health. More articles saying \"health of democracy\" can mean more threat, more advocacy, or one viral op-ed. These series count words."

title: Hand transcription of Rooney Report percents and questionnaire stems, 2026-11-04

# Metadata for data://garden/democracy/2026-11-04/proxies (schema/metadata.schema.yml)
title: Health-of-democracy proxies, GDELT phrase timelines and Rooney Report toplines, as of 2026-11-04
description: >-
  Two kinds of proxy for "health of democracy". GDELT timelines measure
  attention: the share of monitored online news (DOC 2.0) and of national TV
  caption airtime (TV 2.0) that contains a phrase, including Anthropic
  co-mention queries. Rooney toplines are stated attitudes: percents of US
  respondents printed in the text of the Notre Dame Health of Democracy Survey's
  Rooney Reports, each checked against the pinned PDF. None of these series
  measures any effect of Anthropic on democracy. Method and limits in
  docs/democracy-proxies.md.
processing: >-
  `build` reads only saved bytes (no network) and fails if any saved file's
  size, SHA-256 or BLAKE3 differs from MANIFEST.tsv. GDELT: for each of the 24
  planned requests, every timeline point becomes one row of gdelt-timelines.tsv
  (date truncated to YYYYMMDD; value formatted to at most 6 decimals) and each
  series one row of gdelt-summary.tsv; a request never received is kept as a
  NOT PINNED summary row, not dropped, and a `{}` response (no matching clip)
  as an empty-series row. DOC timelinevolraw rows would carry a "(norm)"
  series (GDELT's daily total), but none were pinned. Rooney: each pinned
  report PDF is re-extracted page by page with pypdf 5.4.0 and normalised (NFKC,
  curly quotes, dashes, soft hyphens, whitespace); rooney-reports.tsv records
  page and embedded-image counts and any "AI transparency statement".
  Each hand-transcribed row is checked: the quote must be on its stated page,
  value_text in the quote, and percent in the quote; each hand-copied stem must
  occur in its pinned questionnaire. Any failure stops the build, so the
  toplines and items hold every input row. Drops: chart images (counted, never
  read or estimated), GDELT article and clip text (never requested; no artlist
  mode), and the 7 GDELT requests that returned HTTP 429 (no data, reported as
  NOT PINNED).
unit_of_analysis: >-
  gdelt-timelines.tsv: one (source, query, mode, series, period) value;
  gdelt-summary.tsv: one planned GDELT request and series; rooney-reports.tsv:
  one Rooney Report; rooney-toplines.tsv: one percent printed in report text;
  rooney-items.tsv: one questionnaire item stem.
denominator: >-
  corpus/democracy/gdelt-summary.tsv (all 24 planned GDELT requests, 7 marked
  NOT PINNED); corpus/democracy/rooney-reports.tsv (all 13 reports linked from
  the pinned listing page); corpus/democracy/rooney-transcription.tsv and
  corpus/democracy/rooney-questionnaire.tsv for toplines and items (every input
  row passes or the build fails).
coverage: >-
  GDELT DOC 2.0: daily, 2017-01-01 to 2026-11-03, 3,547 days returned per
  pinned query (days missing from GDELT's response are absent, not zero); 5 of
  12 DOC requests pinned, none of them raw counts, so no DOC article counts or
  daily totals. GDELT TV 2.0: monthly, 2009-07 to 2024-10, 184 months,
  national stations combined; all 12 requests pinned; nothing after October
  2024 is returned. Rooney: 13 reports, October 2024 to May 2026, 129 printed
  values (text layer only; chart figures not extracted); 30 questionnaire stems
  (29 October 2025, 1 May 2026). Earlier waves' questionnaires were not pinned.
  As of 2026-11-04.
does_not_answer:
  - "Whether democracy is healthy: attention is not health. More articles saying \"health of democracy\" can mean more threat, more advocacy, or one viral op-ed. These series count words."
  - "Democratic conditions: Rooney measures what respondents say about norms, not institutions, elections or rights. Stated attitudes are not conditions."
  - "Anything about Anthropic specifically: no series isolates Anthropic. A co-mention count cannot tell praise from criticism, or Anthropic's work on democracy from a reporter's list of AI companies."
  - "Public attitudes to AI or technology companies: Rooney asks nothing about them. Neither pinned questionnaire mentions artificial intelligence, and no pinned report prints the May 2026 DEMOPROB result (the only technology option, \"Social media and misinformation\")."
  - "Causality: even a perfect Anthropic-specific series would show association with attention, not an effect on democratic health."
license:
  name: >-
    Per table: gdelt-*.tsv derive from GDELT data (GDELT terms of use: free use,
    citation and link required); rooney-*.tsv carry short verbatim quotes
    (c) University of Notre Dame, no licence stated. Not CC0.
  url: null
  url_reason: >-
    unknown: GDELT's terms are at https://www.gdeltproject.org/about.html, but
    no licence is stated for the Rooney material or for this folder's derived
    tables (corpus/democracy/README.md). A licence statement from the
    repository owner and the Rooney Democracy Institute would settle it.
status: held
tables:
  corpus/democracy/gdelt-timelines.tsv:
    title: "GDELT phrase timelines, one row per period"
    description: "Every point of every pinned GDELT timeline. Sorted by source, query_id, mode, series, date."
